name: Promvia — AI Traffic Analytics & AI Search Citations
author: promvia

sections.description:
Google Analytics lumps most AI referral traffic into “referral” or “direct”. Promvia separates it: you see how many visitors ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Copilot and Claude sent, which pages they landed on, and whether AI search engines name your site at all.

Promvia shows you two things most analytics tools miss:

  • AI visitors — which assistant (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Copilot, Claude, Grok, Meta AI) sent each visitor, and what they did on your site.
  • Citations — whether those assistants mention or cite your site when people ask the questions your buyers ask, checked on a schedule, with the sources they cite instead of you.

This plugin does four small jobs:

  1. Adds the Promvia pixel to your pages (one <script> tag, loaded defer), with an option to wait for statistics consent through the WP Consent API.
  2. Prints a verification meta tag so Promvia can confirm you own this domain — no DNS record needed.
  3. Creates an application password for Promvia so it can save draft posts to this site (drafts only; nothing is published without you).
  4. Optional — serves the fixes you approve in Promvia without code: Organization structured data (JSON-LD) in your pages’ <head>, your /llms.txt, and the robots.txt lines that let AI search crawlers in. Every visitor sees the same page; nothing is shown only to crawlers.

You need a Promvia account at https://promvia.app. The free plan covers one site and five tracked questions, checked automatically once a month on one AI engine. Paid plans add engines, questions and sites. Promvia does not guarantee any ranking or citation outcome.

Third-party service

This plugin loads https://promvia.app/snippet.js on your public pages, and that script sends page-view events (URL, referrer, a first-party visitor cookie, user agent) to promvia.app, a service operated by Atlaven. No data is sent until you enter a Promvia site id in Settings → Promvia. See the Promvia privacy policy at https://promvia.app/privacy and terms at https://promvia.app/terms. The settings page itself makes no request to promvia.app.

If you paste an “Approved fixes feed” address, your server fetches that address on promvia.app at most every ten minutes to read the fixes you approved. That request comes from your server, not your visitors, and sends nothing about them — only the standard request headers WordPress sends. No request is made until you enter a feed address.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. In Promvia (https://promvia.app/sites), open your site and copy its site id (site_…).
  3. In WordPress go to Settings → Promvia, paste the site id, and save.
  4. Ownership: usually nothing to do — once the pixel is on your home page, Promvia verifies the site by itself. If you load the pixel only after consent, open your site in Promvia → Sites → “Meta tag”, copy the tag, paste it into Settings → Promvia → “Verification token”, save, then press “Verify ownership” in Promvia.
  5. Optional — to let Promvia save drafts: on Settings → Promvia press “Create an application password for Promvia” (HTTPS required) and copy the three values into Promvia → Settings → Integrations → WordPress.
  6. Optional — to publish approved fixes without code: on a fix page in Promvia open “Publish without code”, copy “Your feed address”, paste it into Settings → Promvia → “Approved fixes feed”, and save.
sections.faq:
How do I see traffic from ChatGPT in WordPress?

Install this plugin, then paste your Promvia site id in Settings → Promvia. From then on, visits from ChatGPT appear in Promvia under “AI visitors & revenue”, split by assistant and by landing page. A visit counts whether ChatGPT identifies it with the utm_source=chatgpt.com tag on the link or with chatgpt.com as the referrer.

Is this an SEO plugin?

No. It does not change your titles, meta descriptions or rankings. It measures the traffic AI assistants send you and whether AI search mentions your site (sometimes called generative engine optimization, or GEO). The only things it adds to your pages beyond the pixel and the verification tag are the fixes you approve in Promvia.

Does the pixel slow my site down?

It is one small script loaded with defer, after your page has rendered. It sets a single first-party cookie.

Will it track me while I edit?

By default, no: logged-in users who can edit posts are not tracked. You can turn that off.

Does it work with my cookie banner?

If your consent plugin exposes the WP Consent API (Complianz, CookieYes, Cookiebot and others), tick “Load the pixel only after the visitor consents” and the pixel waits for statistics consent. Without the API, that box means “never load”.

What happens to robots.txt and llms.txt?

Only what WordPress itself serves changes. If your host keeps a real robots.txt or llms.txt file on disk, the web server serves that file and this plugin leaves it alone — add the lines by hand there. In robots.txt only the rules that block the approved AI search crawlers change; every other rule, comment and Sitemap line stays. Training crawlers stay as you set them.

What if Promvia is down?

The plugin keeps serving the last fixes it read. When you stop publishing a fix in Promvia, the plugin stops serving it within about fifteen minutes. When you make a new feed address in Promvia, the old one stops working: paste the new one here.

Can I ask Promvia from ChatGPT or Claude?

Yes. The same data this plugin collects can be read from ChatGPT (Promvia is in ChatGPT’s plugin directory), Claude and other assistants that connect to an MCP server. Sign in with your Promvia account, say “promvia list” to see your sites and “promvia select” followed by a site to choose one; each answer then names the site it is about. Setup steps: https://promvia.app/developers

What does uninstalling remove?

The promvia_settings option and the plugin’s cached copy of your approved fixes. The plugin creates no tables and schedules nothing.
sections.changelog:
1.1.4

  • Plugin name: “AI Search Citations” instead of “ChatGPT Citations” — the free plan checks citations on Perplexity; ChatGPT citation checks come with paid plans. No code changes.

1.1.3

  • Readme: clearer description of AI referral traffic, two new FAQ entries, tags updated. No code changes.

1.1.2

  • Plugin homepage: https://promvia.app/wordpress — setup steps and what each Promvia plan adds.

1.1.1

  • Verification token: pasting the whole meta tag from Promvia → Sites now saves the token inside it.
  • Settings and readme: the ownership step matches Promvia’s current Sites page, and says when it is not needed.
  • FAQ: reading Promvia from ChatGPT or Claude.

1.1.0

  • Approved fixes feed: serve the fixes you approve in Promvia (Organization JSON-LD, llms.txt, robots.txt allow lines for AI search crawlers) without editing code.
  • The pixel and its consent loader are now added through wp_enqueue_script and wp_add_inline_script, and JSON-LD through wp_print_inline_script_tag.

1.0.1

  • Readme: the free plan’s questions are checked automatically once a month (it said weekly).

1.0.0

  • First release: pixel, consent gate, verification meta tag, application-password bridge.
